# Configuring workflows

## Client setup

Each example below is shown for three clients. All three call the same REST API at `https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}/api/v1`; the SDK and the CLI wrap the requests shown in the **curl** tab. Every request requires a bearer token. The deployment’s IAM sidecar validates the token and adds the caller’s user identity to the request, and Sherlock authorizes the request against that identity.

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

Log in once with the platform CLI, then export the deployment URL and a token:

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha iam login    # one-time OAuth login via your browser

export SHERLOCK_URL="https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}"
export AA_TOKEN="$(pharia --env aleph-alpha iam token)"
```

Pass `-H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"` on every call. A platform token from any other source also works; the API only reads the header. Requests with a JSON body use `--json` (curl 7.82.0 or later), which sends the body and sets the `Content-Type` and `Accept` headers to `application/json`. To read the body from a file, use `--json @body.json`.

Install the client from the Aleph Alpha package index:

```bash
pip install sherlock-client --extra-index-url https://alephalpha.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/pypi/holmes/simple
```

Then create a client for the deployment and a handle for the store whose workflows you are configuring:

```python
import os

from sherlock import SyncSherlock

client = SyncSherlock(
    url="https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}",
    token=os.environ["AA_TOKEN"],
)

store = client.v1.search_stores("<store-id>")
```

`url` and `token` default to the `SHERLOCK_BASE_URL` and `SHERLOCK_TOKEN` environment variables, so `SyncSherlock()` without arguments works when those variables are set. `Sherlock` is the async client and has the same API. Use either client as a context manager (`with SyncSherlock(...) as client:`) to close the connection pool when you finish.

The [`pharia`](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/pharia-cli) CLI has a `sherlock` subcommand that covers the full workflow lifecycle. Log in once; every subsequent command uses the cached token:

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha iam login
```

JSON flags accept inline JSON, `@file`, or `@-` for stdin. Select the environment with the global `--env` flag. To reach a different tenant, pass `--base-url` or set `PHARIA_SHERLOCK_URL`.

## Inspecting what exists

List your stores, the workflows on a store, and the current configuration of a single workflow:

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"

curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"

curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows/<workflow-id-or-name>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"
```

```python
for s in client.v1.search_stores.list():
    print(s.id, s.name)

for workflow in store.workflows.list():
    print(workflow.id, workflow.name, workflow.workflow_name)

current = store.workflows("<workflow-id-or-name>").get()
print(current.parameters)
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock stores list
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock workflows list <store-id>
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock workflows get <store-id> <workflow-id-or-name>
```

To read a single workflow, pass either its ID or its name.

## The parameter model

`DocumentAI` consists of modules. Each top-level key in `parameters` configures one module:

| Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `pdf_reader` | Reader for PDF files. `pdf_text` (the default) extracts the embedded text. `pdf_rasterizer` renders pages to images for vision models; pair it with `vision_reader`. `smart_pdf_router` and `pdf_router` decide per page: pages with a usable text layer are extracted as text, and only the other pages are rendered for `vision_reader` (see Recipe: per-page routing). |
| `docx_reader`, `xlsx_reader` | Readers for Word (`.docx`) and Excel (`.xlsx`/`.xlsm`) files. Each has two implementations. The default `doc` and `excel` kinds use anydoc to parse the file into markdown content blocks. The previous `docx` (python-docx) and `xlsx` (openpyxl) kinds remain available. |
| `doc_reader`, `excel_reader`, `pptx_reader`, `markdown_reader`, `html_reader`, `image_reader`, `legacy_office_reader`, `plaintext_reader` | One reader per file type. The workflow routes each document to the matching reader. `doc_reader` reads legacy `.doc` files, and `excel_reader` reads legacy `.xls`/`.xlsb` workbooks. `plaintext_reader` handles all other text files. |
| `vision_reader` | Uses a vision model to annotate rasterized PDF pages. Required when `pdf_reader` is `pdf_rasterizer`, `smart_pdf_router`, or `pdf_router`; not used otherwise. |
| `figure_extractor`, `image_describer` | Optional modules that extract figures from PDF files and describe them with a vision model. |
| `chunker` | Splits pages into chunks. One of `naive`, `fixed_size`, `recursive`, or `markdown`. |
| `page_enrichments`, `chunk_enrichments` | Optional lists of enrichment modules that add metadata to pages or chunks, for example keywords or generated questions. |
| `vectorize` | Embeds chunks and writes vectors to the vector store. |

Groups with more than one implementation (`pdf_reader`, `docx_reader`, `xlsx_reader`, `chunker`) select the implementation with a `"kind"` field. In addition to its own parameters, every module accepts the execution fields `batch_size`, `max_in_flight`, and `timeout`.

## Recipe: text-first ingestion

This is the standard configuration for digitally created documents. It extracts the embedded text, chunks it recursively, and embeds the chunks through the platform’s inference gateway.

```json
{
  "pdf_reader": {"kind": "pdf_text"},
  "chunker": {"kind": "recursive", "chunk_size": 4096, "chunk_overlap": 600},
  "vectorize": {"provider": "pharia"}
}
```

Create a workflow with these parameters and the standard run-input `schema` (see The input schema):

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{
    "name": "text-ingestion",
    "workflow_name": "DocumentAI",
    "parameters": {
      "pdf_reader": {"kind": "pdf_text"},
      "chunker": {"kind": "recursive", "chunk_size": 4096, "chunk_overlap": 600},
      "vectorize": {"provider": "pharia"}
    },
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "properties": {
        "source": {
          "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}],
          "description": "Source path, connector URI, or list thereof"
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

```python
workflow = store.workflows.create(
    name="text-ingestion",
    workflow_name="DocumentAI",
    parameters={
        "pdf_reader": {"kind": "pdf_text"},
        "chunker": {"kind": "recursive", "chunk_size": 4096, "chunk_overlap": 600},
        "vectorize": {"provider": "pharia"},
    },
    schema={
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": True,
        "properties": {
            "source": {
                "anyOf": [
                    {"type": "string"},
                    {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
                ],
                "description": "Source path, connector URI, or list thereof",
            }
        },
    },
)

print(workflow.id)
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock workflows create <store-id> \
  --name text-ingestion \
  --workflow-name DocumentAI \
  --parameters @parameters.json \
  --schema @input-schema.json
```

## Recipe: vision (OCR) ingestion

For scanned documents or complex layouts, rasterize each PDF page and annotate it with a vision model. This pipeline uses two modules. `pdf_rasterizer` renders each page to an image. `vision_reader` converts each image into one structured page, in a separate stage that processes pages in parallel. `pdf_rasterizer` does not extract text, so a `vision_reader` with an explicit `provider` and `model` is required; there is no default endpoint. A run without a `vision_reader`, or with one that lacks `provider` or `model`, fails immediately and is not retried.

```json
{
  "pdf_reader": {"kind": "pdf_rasterizer", "pdf_backend": "pdfboss"},
  "vision_reader": {"provider": "pharia_next", "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr", "timeout": 120},
  "chunker": {"kind": "recursive", "chunk_size": 4096, "chunk_overlap": 600}
}
```

Other `pdf_rasterizer` fields: `pdf_backend` (`pdf_oxide` default, or `pdfboss`), `dpi` (default 150), and `image_format` (default `png`).

Other `vision_reader` fields: `max_tokens`, `temperature` (see Sampling temperature; use `0` for reproducible OCR), `ignore_headers_footers` (default true), `prompt`, and `extra_body`. `prompt` replaces the built-in layout-extraction prompt. By default, dots-OCR models receive a dots-format prompt and other models receive a normalized-coordinate prompt. `extra_body` contains vendor-specific payload fields; for example, `{"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": false}}` disables a reasoning model’s thinking mode. The chunker processes the annotated pages the same way as text-extracted pages.

## Recipe: per-page routing

Many PDFs mix digitally created pages with scanned pages, screenshots, or pages whose fonts do not map to readable characters. `pdf_text` returns empty or garbled text for those pages, and `pdf_rasterizer` sends every page to the vision model, including the pages that `pdf_text` reads correctly. `smart_pdf_router` decides per page. Pages with a usable text layer are extracted as text. Only the other pages are rendered and annotated by `vision_reader`. A mostly digital document therefore costs close to `pdf_text`, and its scanned pages are still read.

```json
{
  "pdf_reader": {"kind": "smart_pdf_router"},
  "vision_reader": {"provider": "pharia_next", "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr", "temperature": 0, "timeout": 120},
  "chunker": {"kind": "recursive", "chunk_size": 4096, "chunk_overlap": 600}
}
```

The router reads the structure of each page (fonts, images, and annotations) without rendering it. A page goes to the vision model when one of these rules applies:

- The page draws images and no fonts, for example a scan.
- The page draws images, and its text layer has fewer than `min_text_chars` non-whitespace characters (default `80`). An example is a screenshot whose text layer contains only a caption or a page number.
- More than `max_unmapped_share` of the page’s non-whitespace text (default `0.02`) is unmapped glyph codes. These are runs of two or more private-use characters or U+FFFD, which fonts without a character map produce. A single symbol, such as a bullet, does not count.
- More than `max_rtl_share` of the page’s non-whitespace text is Arabic or Hebrew letters. The default `1` disables this rule, because the text layer returns right-to-left text in reading order. Set a lower value only if a document’s right-to-left text extracts in the wrong order.

All other pages keep their text layer. A page that draws neither fonts nor images becomes an empty page and is not rendered.

`vision_reader` is required, as in Recipe: vision (OCR) ingestion. A run without it fails before it processes any page and is not retried, even if no page of the document would go to the vision model.

Other `smart_pdf_router` fields:

- `rasterizer` — the rendering settings for the routed pages, with the same fields as `pdf_rasterizer`, for example `{"dpi": 200, "image_format": "png"}`.
- `pdf_backend` — the backend for the structure probe and text extraction. Only `pdfboss` (the default) supports the probe.
- `pages_per_part` (default `10`) — the number of pages that one work item processes.
- `max_in_flight` (default `4`) — the number of text extractions that run at the same time.

`pdf_router` is the basic version of the router. It sends a page to the vision model only when the page draws images and has no extractable text. `smart_pdf_router` with `min_text_chars: 1` and `max_unmapped_share: 1` behaves the same way.

Each page records its routing decision in its metadata under `pdf_router`: `route` (`text` or `raster`), the `fonts`, `images`, and `annotations` counts, and, for each share rule whose limit is below `1`, the page’s measured share (`unmapped_share`, `rtl_share`). Use these values to check why a page went to the vision model.

| | Version availability `pdf_router` is available from release 0.9.0 and `smart_pdf_router` from release 0.10.3. The `max_unmapped_share` and `max_rtl_share` fields are available from release 0.10.8. Older deployments ignore them and do not apply the unmapped-glyph rule. |
|---|---|

## Recipe: figure descriptions (`figure_extractor` + `image_describer`)

Text extraction and OCR do not produce searchable text for the content of charts, diagrams, and photos. The figure pipeline generates text descriptions for them in two stages. A `figure_extractor` produces one image crop per figure. `image_describer` sends each crop to a vision model and stores the returned description.

| | Not yet active Current releases accept these parameter groups but do not run the figure-extraction stage yet, so the pipeline produces no descriptions. The parameters below are stable and are documented ahead of activation. |
|---|---|

```json
{
  "pdf_reader": {"kind": "pdf_rasterizer", "dpi": 200},
  "vision_reader": {"provider": "pharia_next", "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr"},
  "figure_extractor": {"kind": "bbox_figure_extractor", "dpi": 200},
  "image_describer": {
    "provider": "pharia_next",
    "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr",
    "max_tokens": 4096,
    "temperature": 0,
    "extra_body": {"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": false}}
  }
}
```

Two extractors implement `figure_extractor`. Select one with `kind`:

| Kind | Strategy | Pair with |
|---|---|---|
| `figure_extractor` | Extracts the images that are embedded in the PDF file. | `pdf_text` |
| `bbox_figure_extractor` | Renders each page again and crops it at the figure bounding boxes that the vision reader detected. Its `dpi` (default 200) must match the rasterizer’s `dpi`; otherwise the coordinates do not align. The rasterizer default is 150, so set both values explicitly, as in the example above. | `pdf_rasterizer` + `vision_reader` |

`image_describer` fields: `provider` (default `pharia_next`) and `model` (default `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`) identify the vision deployment. `prompt` replaces the built-in description prompt. `max_tokens` (default 2048), `temperature`, and `extra_body` configure the model call. `max_in_flight` (default 4) limits the number of concurrent describe calls.

The platform stores descriptions append-only, keyed by page, image, model, and prompt. A re-run with the same model and prompt has no effect. A different model or prompt adds new descriptions and does not change existing ones.

## Inference providers

Modules that call models (`vision_reader`, `vectorize`, `image_describer`, …​) select their client by name. The `provider` parameter is a lookup key. The endpoint, credentials, and retry policy for each provider are defined in the server-side deployment configuration. Workflow parameters never contain secrets or URLs.

The providers below are available only when the data platform runs on the Aleph Alpha platform. On-premise installations use different providers.

| Provider | Route |
|---|---|
| `pharia` | The platform inference gateway (default). Routes to the legacy backend. |
| `pharia_next` | The same gateway, fixed to the next-generation inference backend. This is the planned long-term route. |
| `d_inference` | A direct connection to the next-generation backend that bypasses the gateway. A temporary route until service-account authentication is available. |
| `openrouter`, `openai` | External OpenAI-compatible endpoints, when the deployment configures them. |

You can select a provider only if the deployment configures it. If you select an unconfigured provider, the run fails.

## Sampling temperature

Every module that calls a chat or vision model accepts a `temperature` field (`0.0`--`2.0`):

- `vision_reader` and `image_reader` — page annotation and image-file reading
- `image_describer` — figure descriptions
- `pdf_reader` with `kind: "parsy_ocr"` — OCR extraction
- `page_enrichments` / `chunk_enrichments` entries that call an LLM, such as `page_questions`

Embeddings (`vectorize`) and non-LLM modules (chunkers, `keyword` enrichment) have no temperature.

If you do not set `temperature` (the default), the request omits the field and the model server’s default applies. `0` is treated as a value and sent to the model; it is not treated as unset. Use `0` for reproducible extraction, which is the usual setting for OCR and structured layout parsing:

```json
{
  "vision_reader": {"provider": "pharia_next", "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr", "temperature": 0}
}
```

| | Version availability `temperature` is available from release 0.8.7. Older deployments accept the field but ignore it. The call uses the server default and does not fail. |
|---|---|

## Choosing a chunker

| Kind | Strategy | Fields (defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| `naive` | Fixed-size word groups with no overlap. Fast, but it can break sentences. | `chunk_size` (1024 words) |
| `fixed_size` | Character-based with overlap. It prefers sentence boundaries. | `chunk_size` (1000 chars), `chunk_overlap` (200), `respect_sentences` (true) |
| `recursive` | Recursive separator hierarchy: paragraphs before line breaks before spaces and punctuation. | `chunk_size` (1024 chars), `chunk_overlap` (200) |
| `markdown` | Splits at top-level markdown blocks. It never splits fenced code, and it prefixes each chunk with its heading breadcrumb. | `chunk_size` (1024 chars), `chunk_overlap` (200) |

Smaller chunks give more precise matches but contain less surrounding context. Overlap preserves context across chunk boundaries.

## Embeddings (`vectorize`)

The `vectorize` module calls an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint through a named provider (default `pharia`; see Inference providers).

The search store defines the vector schema. If you do not set `model` and `dimension`, the module takes them from the store’s `models` entry, so `{"provider": "pharia"}` is usually sufficient. If you set them, they must match a vector configured on the store. If they do not match, the run fails instead of writing vectors that search cannot find.

## Enrichments (`page_enrichments`, `chunk_enrichments`)

Both groups take a **list** of enrichment modules, selected by `kind`. Enrichments add metadata rows for pages or chunks. They do not change the page and chunk content.

| Kind | What it does | Fields (defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| `keyword` | Extracts the top keyword lemmas per item with spaCy. No model call. | `language` (`en` or `de`), `max_keywords` (10), `min_word_length` (3) |
| `page_questions` | Asks an LLM for questions that each page can answer. Useful for HyDE-style retrieval and Q&A dataset generation. Page-level only. | `provider` (`pharia_next`), `model` (`moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`), `num_questions` (5), `max_chars` (4000), `max_tokens` (500), `prompt`, `temperature` |

```json
{
  "page_enrichments": [
    {"kind": "keyword", "language": "de"},
    {"kind": "page_questions", "num_questions": 3, "temperature": 0.7}
  ]
}
```

Removing repeated page headers and footers is not an enrichment. `vision_reader` does it at read time; see Cleaning page headers and footers.

## Cleaning page headers and footers

Repeated headers and footers, such as running titles and page numbers, add irrelevant text to chunks and search hits. `vision_reader` removes them: with `ignore_headers_footers` (default `true`), it skips the header and footer regions that the layout model classifies; see Recipe: vision (OCR) ingestion.

Affected pages record the number of dropped lines as `metadata.headers_footers_removed`.

## The input schema

To create a workflow, you currently must send `schema`: the JSON schema of the input that each run accepts.

| | Deprecation ahead The `schema` property is planned for deprecation. After that, workflow creation will not require it. Until then, pass the standard schema below. |
|---|---|

For `DocumentAI`, the standard schema declares the `source` property:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "properties": {
    "source": {
      "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}],
      "description": "Source path, connector URI, or list thereof"
    }
  }
}
```

## Updating a workflow

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl -X PUT "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows/<workflow-id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{
    "parameters": {
      "pdf_reader": {"kind": "pdf_rasterizer", "pdf_backend": "pdfboss"},
      "vision_reader": {"provider": "pharia_next", "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr", "timeout": 120},
      "chunker": {"kind": "recursive", "chunk_size": 4096, "chunk_overlap": 600}
    }
  }'
```

This body switches the workflow created above to the vision configuration. It contains the whole `parameters` document, with `pdf_reader` changed and a `vision_reader` group added.

```python
store.workflows("<workflow-id>").update(
    parameters={
        "pdf_reader": {"kind": "pdf_rasterizer", "pdf_backend": "pdfboss"},
        "vision_reader": {
            "provider": "pharia_next",
            "model": "rednote-hilab/dots.mocr",
            "timeout": 120,
        },
        "chunker": {"kind": "recursive", "chunk_size": 4096, "chunk_overlap": 600},
    },
)
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock workflows update <store-id> <workflow-id> \
  --parameters @parameters.json
```

| | Updates replace, not merge `update` replaces the entire `parameters` object. First read the current configuration (see Inspecting what exists). Then edit it and send the full document. If you send only the changed group, all other overrides are removed. |
|---|---|

The change applies only to future runs. The platform does not automatically reprocess content that is already indexed.

## Running and watching

To start a run, specify a source (file IDs from [Ingesting files](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/ingesting-files.html)). Then stream its progress:

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows/<workflow-id>/runs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{"input": {"source": ["files://<file-id>"]}}'

curl -N "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows/<workflow-id>/runs/<run-id>/event-stream" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"

curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/workflows/<workflow-id>/runs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"
```

```python
runs = store.workflows("<workflow-id>").runs

run = runs.execute(input={"source": ["files://<file-id>"]})

for event in run.stream():
    print(event.event, event.data)

for past in runs.list():
    print(past.id, past.status)
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock runs execute <store-id> <workflow-id> \
  --input '{"source": ["files://<file-id>"]}'

pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock runs watch <store-id> <workflow-id> <run-id>
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock runs list <store-id> <workflow-id>
```

The event stream sends server-sent events until the run completes or fails. Deleting a workflow also deletes all its runs and their derived data.

- [Workflows and presets](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/workflows-and-presets.html) — the built-in presets and how to select one.
- [For workflow authors](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/workflow-authors.html) — how to write workflow classes and modules in code.
